chunks: From him, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Abī al-Mighrāʾ, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم gave permission to the women and children to depart by night, to stone the jamarāt by night, and to perform the morning prayer in their lodgings. And if the women feared menstruation, they could proceed to Makkah and appoint someone to perform the sacrifice on their behalf.

key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: the ritual stone-pillars pelted during hajj
key_terms.الْحَيْضَ: menstruation, affecting ritual rulings for women
key_terms.رَخَّصَ: granted a legal concession or dispensation
key_terms.لِلنِّسَاءِ: for women, specifically in the context of hajj rulings
key_terms.وَالصِّبْيَانِ: and children, included in the concession
key_terms.يُفِيضُوا: to depart from al-Muzdalifah and move onward in the hajj rites

ai.seo_question: What concession did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم give to women and children for leaving al-Muzdalifah before dawn?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal concession granted by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم for women and children during the rites of hajj. It allows them to leave al-Muzdalifah at night, perform the stoning at night, pray the morning prayer in their dwellings, and, in the case of women fearing menstruation, proceed to Makkah and appoint a representative for the sacrifice.
